profiles.notes: Undated official guidance checked 18 October 2026; not a confirmed current-year offer. Qualification routes are alternatives, not cumulative requirements.

requirements.label: Complete and submit the application
requirements.details: Register in the application portal, complete the requested information and supporting uploads, then submit. An application saved without final submission is not evaluated. Undergraduate paper applications may instead be emailed or delivered in person.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: High-school transcripts and qualifying results
requirements.details: Submit high-school transcripts with one accepted school-leaving qualification. Alternative qualification routes are described separately; applicants awaiting results can use the pending-results procedure.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: WASSCE: six subjects at C6 or better
requirements.details: For the WASSCE route, the six subjects are Integrated Science, Core Mathematics, Core English and three electives; each must be at least C6. This is not an IB score or a guarantee of admission.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: A-level and IGCSE/O-level route
requirements.details: At least three A-level passes, each in the A-D grade range, together with six IGCSE/GCE O-level passes including Mathematics, English and Science.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Engineering: Physics and further mathematics
requirements.details: Applicants intending to major in Engineering must have taken Physics and Elective/Further Mathematics. The FAQ does not give qualification-specific grade thresholds for these subjects.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: American or Canadian high-school diploma
requirements.details: An American or Canadian High School Diploma is an accepted alternative school-leaving qualification. This page does not state an AP, SAT, ACT or GPA threshold for this route.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: French Baccalaureate route
requirements.details: The French Baccalaureate is accepted with a certified original score copy and a certified English translation. No numerical Baccalaureate threshold is stated here.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Other approved examination qualifications
requirements.details: Equivalent examination results approved by the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission can be considered; the FAQ does not list a universal conversion score.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Personal essay in application review
requirements.details: The FAQ identifies the personal essay as part of the application reviewed before final examination results arrive. It does not specify a current essay prompt, count or word limit; the separately dated 2024/25 paper form must not be treated as the current portal.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Extracurricular activities in review
requirements.details: Extracurricular activities form part of the early application review. No required competition, prize, activity count or award level is stated.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Interview for shortlisted candidates
requirements.details: Submitted applications are reviewed and shortlisted candidates are invited to a personal interview. The decision uses both the application and interview; this is not a compulsory interview for every initial applicant.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Apply while awaiting examination results
requirements.details: An applicant awaiting WASSCE, A-level, IB or equivalent examination results may apply first, then reopen the application, add results and resubmit when available. Early review is not final admission without the results.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Update accomplishments and awards
requirements.details: After submission, applicants may add new accomplishments or awards through their admissions account and resubmit, or email admissions. This permission does not establish a compulsory competition or award requirement.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Proof of application payment
requirements.details: The admissions office says processing is completed only after proof of payment is received. A fee-waiver request is a separate reviewed procedure; no automatic waiver is promised.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Requesting an application-fee waiver
requirements.details: Applicants unable to afford the application fee may email admissions@ashesi.edu.gh. Eligibility is reviewed using responses to a short questionnaire; requesting a waiver does not guarantee approval.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

profiles.notes: Additional international requirements appear in both undergraduate and graduate FAQ sections and are stored once here. They supplement the applicable degree/route requirements; no numerical English score is inferred.

requirements.details: International applicants must provide certified translations of non-English transcripts or supporting documents as copies of the originals. The French Baccalaureate's specific certification rule is already stated in its shared qualification route.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: English evidence when high school was not English-medium
requirements.details: International applicants whose high-school instruction was not in English must supply English-proficiency evidence, such as TOEFL or IELTS. The FAQ states no test minimum, subscore or validity period.

source.title: Ashesi: How to Apply and admissions FAQ

requirements.label: Application form and declaration
requirements.details: Apply online or using the admission application form; submit the required documents with a signed form and declare the information supplied is true. Handbook clause 11.1.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: Certified identity/citizenship evidence
requirements.details: Provide a certified birth certificate, passport or other legal identity document showing name, birth date and citizenship. Where the current name differs, include legal name-change evidence.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: Certified qualifications and transcripts
requirements.details: Provide certified copies of educational qualifications and transcripts. USP may request additional documents; the handbook does not make an essay or competition record universally compulsory.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: Accurate application evidence
requirements.details: USP may refuse or cancel admission if supporting evidence is untrue or misleading. Under clause 11.2, an applicant whose admission is declined or cancelled on this ground may reapply after one semester with correct evidence.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: Normally one programme at a time
requirements.details: Clause 11.1 normally disallows concurrent admission to more than one programme; no universal exception or approval entitlement is inferred.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

profiles.notes: 2026 handbook printed pages 78-79 / PDF 79-80. International = citizenship outside USP member countries. Language pathways supplement academic equivalencies; programme/level thresholds remain separate.

requirements.label: When English-proficiency evidence is needed
requirements.details: International applicants whose entry qualification was not taught in English must meet the English requirement. In this handbook, international means citizens of non-USP-member countries, not every person who is non-Fijian.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: Language-test results: within two years
requirements.details: When examination scores establish English proficiency, results must have been obtained within two years of the admission application date. Published alternatives are not cumulative test requirements.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: Unclassified study where English is not yet sufficient
requirements.details: An applicant meeting all other admission requirements but not the English condition may be admitted to an Unclassified Programme. This is not direct unconditional admission to the requested degree.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: Pakistan intermediate / tertiary route: international qualification route
requirements.details: Complete HSSC Intermediate Division 1 with average 65% in four subjects, or successfully complete the first year of a degree at a recognized tertiary institution. Academic-equivalency guideline for diploma/undergraduate entry, not guaranteed admission.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: Papua New Guinea HSC: international qualification route
requirements.details: Complete the Higher School Certificate with a B grade average. Academic-equivalency guideline for diploma/undergraduate entry, not guaranteed admission.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: USA diploma / tertiary route: international qualification route
requirements.details: Complete an accredited honours or college-preparatory high-school diploma, or successfully complete the first year at an accredited tertiary institution. This row states no SAT, ACT or AP threshold; absence is not a test-not-required policy. Academic-equivalency guideline for diploma/undergraduate entry, not guaranteed admission.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

profiles.notes: Mature-entry route, handbook clauses 4.3.12 and 11.3, printed pages 78 and 95. Not an automatic waiver of course prerequisites or a general first-year age policy.

requirements.label: Mature admission: background and experience
requirements.details: Under clause 11.3, Senate or its delegate considers likelihood of successful completion using academic background and the nature of employment/experience. No universal age or years-of-experience cutoff is stated in this clause.

source.title: USP 2026 Handbook: admission regulations, printed pages 78-84 and 95

requirements.label: Mature admission: prescribed prerequisite courses
requirements.details: A mature applicant may be required to pass courses prescribed by Senate or its delegate for the specific programme. Equivalent entry qualifications completed more than five years ago may also be considered through mature entry.
